Reassembly tree management, insertion, query, publish, and debug print functions.

# Purpose
This C file implements the main runtime logic for `fd_reasm`, a Merkle-tree reassembler for FEC blocks. It defines the object layout and life-cycle functions [`fd_reasm_align`](<#fd_reasm_align>), [`fd_reasm_footprint`](<#fd_reasm_footprint>), [`fd_reasm_new`](<#fd_reasm_new>), [`fd_reasm_join`](<#fd_reasm_join>), [`fd_reasm_leave`](<#fd_reasm_leave>), and [`fd_reasm_delete`](<#fd_reasm_delete>), which allocate and attach the reassembler inside shared memory. The object contains several internal data structures, including `pool`, `ancestry`, `frontier`, `orphaned`, `subtrees`, `bfs`, `out`, and `slot_mr`, which the code uses to track connected nodes, orphaned nodes, pending output, and slot-to-block metadata.

The file also defines the core tree operations used by the reassembler. [`fd_reasm_insert`](<#fd_reasm_insert>) adds a new FEC node, links it to a parent when the parent is known, stores orphaned nodes when the parent is not known, and later connects children by using slot metadata and chained Merkle roots. [`fd_reasm_publish`](<#fd_reasm_publish>) changes the active root and removes nodes that are no longer part of the published tree. Helper functions such as [`fd_reasm_query`](<#fd_reasm_query>), [`fd_reasm_peek`](<#fd_reasm_peek>), [`fd_reasm_out`](<#fd_reasm_out>), and the parent and child accessors provide read access to the internal tree state. The file ends with [`fd_reasm_print`](<#fd_reasm_print>), which prints the current frontier and subtree state for debugging.
